newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up, bull run continues on GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up, bull run continues on GDP growth.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed higher for the sixth consecutive session Tuesday, pushed up by the release of strong economic growth figures, brokers said.
They added the market could continue rising Wednesday because of pending buy-orders but was also overdue a technical correction, as investors were looking to take profits on their recent gains.
Tuesday, the General Index rose 0.44 percent to 1,685.61 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.62 percent to 2,438.71 points.
In a total of 2,284 trades, volume was 36.0 million soles ($13.6 million), according to preliminary figures.
The economy grew 4.5 percent year-on-year in January, compared with a contraction of 2.2 percent in January 1996, President Alberto Fujimori said midway through Monday's session.
"The production (announcement) immediately pushed up indutrial stocks enlivening the session," Pablo Navarro of local brokerage Fortuna said.
Backus y Johnston, the country's largest brewery rose 1.56 percent to 2.60 soles in volume of 614,000 shares.
Electricity distributor, Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- rose 0.79 percent to 1.27 soles, on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Benchmark Telefnica del Per "B" remained stable at 6.08 soles, also in volume of 1.1 million shares.
